name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district with a -21 point partisan lean
Incumbent David Taylor is running and has raised over $1 million
Democratic challenger has no reported fundraising or polling presence
Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 98 percent
model.rationale: This southwestern Ohio seat sits about twenty-one points to the right of the country, and first-term incumbent David Taylor is running for another term with a solid fundraising edge while the Democratic challenger shows no measurable campaign infrastructure. With no competitive polling and markets pricing a Republican win near certainty, the fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent victory.
model.watch: A major scandal, an unexpected incumbent retirement, or a surge of outside spending against Taylor would be the main ways this race could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 2nd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about twenty-one points toward the GOP. David Taylor, the incumbent Republican, is running for reelection and has raised roughly $1.1 million with about $443,000 on hand. His Democratic opponent, Jennifer Mazzuckelli, has no reported fundraising on file.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert race raters have flagged the contest as competitive. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes this a safe Republican seat, with the Democratic challenger facing an uphill fight that would require extraordinary outside developments to change.
